strengths: The paper introduces a well-motivated and elegant formulation that integrates temporal abstractions (the options framework) into the Successor Representation (SR), effectively addressing the core policy-dependency bottleneck of classical SR.
The theoretical foundation is solid. The authors derive the recursive HSR Bellman operator and provide a rigorous proof that it is a contraction mapping under the max-norm (Theorem 3.1).

An insightful analysis of the geometry of HSR is presented. The authors demonstrate that HSR preserves intra-compartment dispersion (avoiding the 'topological collapse' of classical SR), which uniquely makes it amenable to Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) to yield sparse, localized, and highly interpretable features.

The paper is exceptionally well-written, with highly informative figures, clear schematics, and comprehensive experimental evaluations across multiple transfer-learning, GPI, and intrinsic exploration tasks.
weaknesses: The empirical evaluation is limited to discrete, tabular grid-world environments. While this is helpful for isolating representational properties, it remains to be seen how well HSR scales to continuous state spaces or high-dimensional environments where deep neural networks are required.

The HSR framework relies heavily on a multi-stage pipeline (eigenoption discovery via SVD, learning option-specific policies, expected HSR estimation, and NMF factorization), which is computationally intensive and complex compared to end-to-end model-free RL representation learning methods.

The authors demonstrate that classical SR suffers from topological collapse (making NMF ill-posed), whereas HSR's piecewise-smooth topology is uniquely compatible with NMF to discover sparse, interpretable, and localized bottleneck representations.

Comprehensive empirical evaluations, showing robust transfer across various gridworld topologies, option budgets, and compatibility with Generalised Policy Improvement (GPI) and intrinsic exploration.
Excellent writing, clear schematic diagrams, and highly intuitive visualizations that effectively communicate the core concepts.
weaknesses: The experimental validation is limited to discrete, tabular gridworld environments. While this is helpful for isolating structural and topological representation properties, the performance of the method in high-dimensional or continuous state spaces using deep neural networks remains untested.

The overall framework is algorithmically complex, requiring multiple distinct phases: discovering eigenoptions, training option-specific policies, solving/updating the HSR, and performing non-negative matrix factorization (NMF).

strengths: Elegant conceptual framework that successfully integrates temporal abstraction (options) with the successor representation (SR) to mitigate policy dependence and spectral diffusion.
Solid theoretical support, including a proof that the Hierarchical Successor Representation (HSR) Bellman operator is a contraction mapping (Theorem 3.1), enabling standard TD-learning methods.

Insightful analysis of the representation's geometry, demonstrating why non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) succeeds on HSR (by capturing piecewise-smooth manifold structures) but fails on classic SR (due to topological feature collapse).

Thorough empirical evaluation across several domains and tasks, demonstrating improvements in robust transfer, out-of-distribution value function reconstruction, integration with Generalised Policy Improvement (GPI), and intrinsically motivated exploration.
weaknesses: The experimental validation is limited entirely to discrete, tabular grid-world environments, leaving the scalability and stability of HSR in continuous state-action spaces and deep RL settings unverified.

The proposed offline pipeline is computationally heavy, requiring multi-stage optimization (eigenoption discovery, learning option policies, analytical HSR solving, and NMF optimization) which may not scale efficiently to larger environments.

The performance and quality of the HSR remain highly dependent on the quality of the temporal abstraction; in scenarios where discovering meaningful options is difficult, the advantages of the framework may degrade.
The exploration experiments would be stronger if compared against standard hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) baselines or non-SR-based state-of-the-art flat exploration methods.
